"Whats this?" Char'li exlaimed, marveling at the smooth flat object protruding from the cavern wall. Clearing soil from around the object the young Med'ja dislodged the unusual object from its resting place and turned it over in his hands. The object was a small round disk which fitted neatly in the young Med'ja's palm, it had a smooth and rounded edge that felt strange to the touch bordered by two equally flat sides with a flawless mirrored finish.

"It's a stone" replied Sha'ne, den mate to the young Char'li. "But it is unlike any stone seen before" her comrade countered "its shape is that of the moon and it is as smooth as the stillest of waters" "Then it is a strange stone" Sha'ne quipped back "Maybe you shall become as strange as that stone and go up to join the Shamans?" Char'li's cheeks began to burn as a wave of laughter rippled throughout the group of young workers. Placing the coin into a small pouch he kept at his side Char'li returned to digging away at the wall cursing his den mates stupidity under his breath "Is she not intrigued by the mystery of the stone?, How could she not be? Was it a gift from the gods or an omen of some disaster yet to befall them?"

That night as he lay in his nest, the stone secured snuggly within, Char'li reasoned that the stone was indeed a gift from the gods and that since he was the one to uncover it he would keep the stone as close as possible, lest the god believe he was rejecting their gift.

One day while Char'li was working in the Burrows southern tunnels a tremor ran through the earth. Though the Med'ja had learned to strengthen their tunnels against such disturbances the tunnel in which Char'li worked was new and had yet to be reinforced by the techniques of the Elders. Char'li fled as the ground shook and the air began to fill with the rain of falling soil. As he approached the exit a large rock fell from the roof above threatening to crush the young Med'ja beneath its weight.

Char'li dove to the side, his ears ringing as he struck the tunnel wall mid-flight. His body crumpling to the floor as the rock slammed down beside him. As his vision began to grow dark Char'li prayed that the gods were indeed watching over him.

Char'li's mind slipped deep into the darkness and as it did he dreamt of dirt, of rock and of a thousand grabbing hands.

Waking he found himself back in his nest surrounded by his mother and several denmates. "Thank Yuna you're awake!" his mother cried, holding the young Med'ja's head to her breast "What happened?" Char'li asked groggily "The ground shook" Sha'ne replied, holding her tail nervously "The tunnel collapsed, you were buried for so long the Shaman wasn't sure you'd make it"

Char'li nodded and closed his eyes, trying to remember. "I remember the tunnel, a large rock..." suddenly he lurched forward breaking free from his mother's embrace "My Pouch!" he cried "Did anybody find my pouch?!"

"It was found in the tunnel when they pulled you out but I'm afraid it was damaged during the collapse" Char'li's mother handed him the small, dirt stained pouch which now had a large tear in the side. "The stone is gone" he stated sadly lowering back against his nest. Char'li felt as though he might cry.

"What are you talking about my dear?" Char'li's mother asked, concered that perhaps the tunnel's collapse had damaged his head. "I found a strange stone when Sha'ne and I were extending the mushroom cave walls, it was a gift from the Gods, as round as the moon and as beautiful as starlight"

"The will of the Gods is unknowable" Char'li's mother consoled "Perhaps the stone was meant to protect you, and, now that it has, returned to its master" Char'li did not agree with his mother though he did not say so out loud, after all why would the Gods bestow a gift only to take it away? Surely it must be back in the tunnel, waiting beneath the earth for Char'li to retrieve it.

Time passed and Char'li's strength slowly returned, all the while his mind was preoccupied with thoughts of the stone's retrieval. One day he rose, the aches and protests of his body having passed and found that his mother, using needle of bone and thread of grass had repaired the tear inflicted on his pouch by the tunnel's collapse. He raised it up, noting that it was heavier than he expected and upon opening the bag and made a remarkable discovery.

Unbidden and seemingly without assistance, the stone had returned.
